title: NOX METALS vs Yarde Metals for Aerospace Aluminum Plate
summary: Yarde Metals holds AS9100 Rev D with Boeing, Lockheed Martin, and Gulfstream approvals. NOX METALS holds ISO 9001:2015 with instant pricing and certs on every order. The honest comparison, including where Yarde wins.
body_markdown:
### Is NOX METALS AS9100 certified?


No. We hold ISO 9001:2015, published with scope at noxmetals.co/verified. Yarde Metals holds AS9100 Rev D. If your program requires AS9100 at the distributor level, buy from an AS9100-registered distributor.


### What is the difference between ISO 9001 and AS9100?


AS9100 is built on top of ISO 9001 and adds aerospace-specific requirements including risk management, configuration management, and counterfeit part prevention. ISO 9001:2015 covers the quality management system generally. Many aerospace programs require AS9100 at the manufacturer and accept ISO 9001 at the distributor, but the requirement is program-specific and you should read your purchase order.


### Does Yarde Metals show prices online?


No. Their cart produces a quotation rather than a published price, and mill certs are accessed through a customer portal login. Our pricing is published and instant, and certs ship with the order.


### Who stocks more aerospace aluminum alloys?


Yarde has the broader list, including 2024 and a long roster of cast tool and jig trade names such as ALCA-5, K100-S, MIC-6, QC-10 and QC-7. We are deliberately narrower: 6061, 7075, 7050, 5000-series, and cast tool and jig, stocked deep in thick sections and with DFARS options.


### Which one is better for a DFARS flow-down?


A DFARS 252.225-7009 clause asks where the metal was melted, which is a melt-source documentation question rather than a quality-system question. We stock DFARS-compliant and domestic-melt material across 6061, 7075 and 7050 as a standing offering. Yarde does not publicly market melt-source documentation, so ask them directly and get the answer in writing.
